title: Long AVGO — Chip-Curb Relative Winner + Q3 FY2026 AI ASIC Earnings
entry: Initiate $430-448 today; enter on any intraday pullback from the $448.88 intraday high toward $432-438. Scale: 70% at current zone; 30% add on a confirmed close above $450 on volume. This is a fresh entry after the prior AVGO position (long-avgo-ai-custom-asic-nvda-readthrough-2026-05-26) hit Target 1 ($440) intraday today — the new position is initiated with a higher thesis anchor (chip-curb exemption + Q3 earnings catalyst) and different targets.
stop_loss: $415 daily close (~5.7% below entry midpoint $440) — implies the DELL AI server blowout read-through reverses, OR Broadcom guides Q3 FY2026 AI ASIC revenue below $4.5B at late-July earnings, OR NVDA breaks $210 daily close pulling the entire AI semis complex lower
targets: $475 — Broadcom Q3 FY2026 earnings preview period (July); AI ASIC revenue run-rate confirmed above $5B quarterly; chip-curb creates incremental enterprise budget shift toward AVGO XPUs; +8.0%
$515 — Q3 FY2026 earnings beat (late July/August): AI ASIC revenue $5.5B+ (vs. $4.7B guide), +80%+ YoY; management raises FY2026 AI guide above $22B; +17.0%

$565 — Full chip-curb winner re-rating: AVGO explicitly cited in hyperscaler communications as the preferred AI inference chip after NVDA Blackwell export restrictions; analyst consensus moves to $540+; +28.4%
catalyst: The US Commerce Department's Malaysia AI chip loophole closure (June 1) explicitly targets NVDA Blackwell GPUs and AMD MI350x — general-purpose GPU architectures shipped to Chinese-controlled entities outside China. Broadcom's custom AI accelerators (XPUs) for Google TPU v5p, Meta MTIA v2, Apple Neural Engine, and ByteDance are architecturally and legally exempt: these are co-designed ASICs under multi-year license agreements held by US parent companies, not subject to the entity-list restriction. The morning briefing explicitly noted 'AVGO $425-448 — less directly exposed to the Malaysia loophole; hold for June earnings catalyst.' The Q3 FY2026 earnings (late July) catalyzes the next leg: Broadcom guided $4.7B AI revenue for Q2 ($47B annualized run-rate), and Q3 is the first quarter where the DELL-confirmed hyperscaler AI capex surge ($24.4B in a single quarter of DELL AI server orders) translates into Broadcom XPU deployment demand.
thesis:
Broadcom holds a unique position in the June 1 regime: it is the only major AI semiconductor company that benefits from the AI capex acceleration (hyperscaler demand) while being structurally exempt from the chip-curb export restrictions (US-hyperscaler-only customer base). NVDA and AMD both face revenue headwinds from the Malaysia loophole closure; Broadcom's XPU revenue from Google, Meta, Apple, and ByteDance US data centers is entirely unaffected. This creates a new relative-value argument: if hyperscalers must redirect AI budget from NVDA Blackwell allocations (constrained by export rules) toward alternative inference compute, AVGO XPUs are the primary beneficiary.

The Q3 FY2026 earnings catalyst is 7-8 weeks away (late July). Broadcom reported Q2 FY2026 AI ASIC revenue of $4.7B (guided), +46% YoY. Q3 guidance implied continued acceleration. The DELL blowout on May 29 ($51.3B AI server backlog, $24.4B in new AI orders in a single quarter) provides external validation that hyperscaler AI infrastructure deployment is accelerating faster than Broadcom's conservative guidance assumed. Every dollar of hyperscaler AI inference workload running on Google Cloud, AWS, Meta's data centers, or Apple's iCloud AI infrastructure runs on Broadcom custom silicon. The chip-curb does not slow this; it accelerates the structural allocation toward US-based inference compute.

The entry today is at Target 1 of the prior AVGO opportunity ($440), which represents the prior quick-profit-take level. For this new position, Target 1 is set at $475 (previously Target 2 of the May 26 position), acknowledging that the entry price is higher and the next confirmation requires Q3 earnings visibility. The stop at $415 is tighter than the original position's $390 stop — appropriate given the higher entry price and the fact that this is a thesis-continuation trade, not a fresh value entry.

The bear-counter-party is the analyst who argues that Broadcom's XPU revenue is too concentrated in three customers (Google 40%, Meta 20%, Apple 15%) and that any capex pullback by one hyperscaler creates outsized concentration risk. This is a real risk — AVGO does not have NVDA's 3,000+ customer diversification. However, the chip-curb creates a short-term narrative where concentration becomes a feature, not a bug: Broadcom's three largest customers are all US-domiciled and entirely unaffected by any export restriction scenario.
bull_case: Q3 FY2026 earnings (late July): AI ASIC revenue $5.5B+ vs. $4.7B guide (+17% beat); management raises FY2026 AI guide from $20B to $23B+. Broadcom is explicitly cited in Google Cloud or Meta capex disclosures as the primary inference chip vendor for their AI expansion. The chip-curb narrative drives a sustained institutional preference for AVGO over NVDA — AVGO earns a 'clean AI' premium multiple of 38x forward earnings. Stock to $515 (Target 2) within 6 weeks. Tail: Apple announces a 30% increase in Neural Engine deployment for Apple Intelligence — AVGO captures the mobile-AI inference upgrade cycle as a $3B+ additional revenue stream.
bear_case: The chip-curb rule's scope is narrowed by Commerce guidance to exclude inference workloads entirely, eliminating the 'AVGO relative winner' narrative. Broadcom Q3 guidance disappoints at $4.8B (vs. $5.0B+ expected), implying hyperscaler AI ASIC demand is front-loaded and decelerating. Meta announces partial in-house MTIA manufacturing (removing AVGO from a portion of Meta's inference stack). The $415 stop triggered within 3 weeks on fundamental disappointment. Structurally: if the chip-curb rule is eventually repealed, the relative-winner narrative that drove the gap fully reverses.
invalidation: $415 daily close, OR Broadcom guides Q3 FY2026 AI ASIC revenue below $4.5B at late-July earnings, OR a hyperscaler announces an in-house inference chip replacing Broadcom for a material workload portion, OR the chip-curb rule is narrowed to exclude inference workloads
